paragraphs: Rav Shmuel son of Rav Abahu. Hyman describes his father, Rav Abahu, as having been one of the heads of the kallah (רישי כלי) of Rafram (the second), according to the testimony of his son Rav Shmuel in Chullin 49a. And Hyman reports that it is stated explicitly in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, end of chapter 3, that Rafram held office in Pumbedita from the year 644 (תרמ״ד) until 754 (תשנ״ד), and in the Raavad’s Sefer HaKabbalah that he died in 756 (תשנ״ו). And his son Rav Shmuel was already

considered among the heads of the Savoraic rabbis (רבנן סבוראי). He is mentioned further in the Gemara, as in Chullin 59b: 'That karkoz (כרכוז) goat that was in the house of the Exilarch — Rav Achai forbade it; Rav Shmuel son of Rav Abahu ate of it, applying to himself [the verse] "From the fruit of a man's mouth his soul (נפשו) shall be satisfied."' And in Avodah Zarah 69 [printed ע״ז סט, with comma; amud unresolved]: 'Rav Achai assessed with vinegar at fifty; Rav Shmuel son of Rav Ika

assessed with beer at sixty.' The reading reported from Dikdukei Soferim, Halakhot Gedolot and Tosafot is: Rav Hai, [and] Rav Shmuel son of Rav Abahu. And Hyman reports from the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, in the edition designated ב״ג: that in the year 808 (תת״ח), in Kislev, Rav Shmuel bar Abahu of Pum Beditha died. And other versions read Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah.

And what we find in Midrash Shmuel, at the supplied locator פ״ידה: 'R' Shmuel son of R' Abahu said: An elder in whom a matter of disgrace was found is not demoted' — Hyman regards this as a scribal error and says it should read R' Shmuel bar Nachmani.

The whole printed notice spans volume III, pp. 1133–1134. The whole Chullin 49a passage calls the father Rabbi Abbahu, beside Hyman’s Rav Abahu, and supports the heads-of-kallah report without proving the Savoraic classification or chronology. Chullin 59b likewise has Rabbi Abbahu. Its quoted verse says “his belly” (בטנו), whereas Hyman’s supplied quotation says “his soul” (נפשו); the English preserves Hyman’s soul wording and discloses this difference. The fuller fat discussion and subsequent ruling are not inserted into his abridgement. Avodah Zarah 69a directly has Rav Achai, Rav Shmuel son of Rav Ika, vinegar at fifty and beer at sixty. Hyman’s alternative Hai/Abahu readings from Dikdukei Soferim, Halakhot Gedolot and Tosafot remain attributed; the bounded Tosafot check did not establish the reported variant and is not evidence of absence. The whole Oxford 1888 Epistle passage has Gabiha’s death in 744 followed by Rafram’s death in 754; it does not establish Hyman’s office start in 644 or his reported Sefer HaKabbalah death in 756. Another whole Oxford passage names Shmuel bar Yehudah of Pumbedita dying in Kislev 817, beside Hyman’s 808/Abahu report from the unidentified ב״ג printing. No era, missing millennium or chronological repair is supplied. The whole consulted Midrash Shmuel 7:5, in the Krakow 1893 digital text, explicitly attributes the elder’s non-demotion statement to Rabbi Shmuel bar Rabbi Abbahu. This supports the reported base reading, not Hyman’s definite proposal to correct it to Shmuel bar Nachmani. His literal פ״ידה locator remains alongside this comparison, without a claim about its exact decoding or the identity of the speaker. All current notes and Hebrew remain unchanged; earlier pending-source statements are retained as the record of those earlier reviews.
